title: Large personal Amiga/DOS simulation and native application discovery
summary: Personally screen 757 candidate URLs and add 19 projects, with five explicit non-promotion decisions.
notes: Root personally searched 12 GitHub query routes across Amiga, Atari ST, CPC and DOS, screened 757 unique URLs and inspected 24 pinned trees. Nineteen additions and five explicit non-promotions. Source releases, derived ports, partial format readers, game-language VMs and instruction-level emulation are differentiated. No upstream game, compiler, installer, emulator or hardware program executed.

sources.reason: Structured native game engine with original Amiga disk resource decoding and original-layout saves; inspected Grudge Night logic citing recovered routines. DOS editions supply optional SE cars and audio, not an asserted separately recovered DOS engine.

Builds on Kylofon v0.1.0 native DOS port, adding switchable EGA/CGA/Hercules/Amiga presentation and Amiga Northern Germany scenery. Pinned recovery code retains bounded original register/segment model for differential tests.
Render-free Rust port of OpenBounty Kings Bounty reconstruction with macroquad shell; inspected structured army/combat rules and determinism-coupled limits.

Semantic Python simulation and UI follow original assembly through source-line/address citations. Inspected structured tribes/people fields and corrected battle/magnet logic, not a generic 68000 dispatch loop.
Native ball/physics/rules structures guided by historical source, with original PRG files read as data and x86 never executed. Inspected fixed-width ball state and synchronization callbacks.
Alien Breed SE92, II and Tower Assault asset readers/editor plus ECS engine. Inspected MAPReader handling big-endian chunks and three format identities; EPF and ACBM/SPR/BLK resources supported.
Source-derived Qt6 redesign of Eric Totels MUI-Builder2.3; inspected original version-tag loader mapping and MUIB record parsing. Generates Amiga MUI C source.
Go/Ebiten source translation from memmaker lands-of-lore-1-re, with structured combat factors and original routine references. EMC/TIM/AV are recovered game-script VMs, not x86 execution.
Watcom10 LE/DOS4GW recovery with304 assembly segments and977 of1084 functions reported C-matched. Inspected actual DrawFrameSprite C and C progress ledger.
Original decompiler output incrementally receives real types, native allocation and SDL3 service boundary. Inspected startup/game function recovery rather than instruction-dispatch emulation.
Readable soft-body vehicle simulation derived from original assembly and Win16 port; inspected structured mass-point/spring physics rather than mechanical instruction wrappers.
Native engine/editor uses decoded SKYNET.EXE tables and AIS scripts, with prior Godot port as reference. Inspected structured enemy families and original-address perception constants.
Function-by-function simulation/frontend/debrief recovery, inspected original-address-cited award/ribbon implementation. Native services with OPL audio chip model, not original CPU runtime.
Native recovered/partly rewritten engine with debug-symbol-assisted function identification. Inspected structured car state and bounded numeric conversion, not original x86 execution.
C++20 DAX/GEO/ECL readers and typed ECL interpreter with terminal exploration and mod overlay framework. Inspected bounded operand/memory access semantics and explicit host callbacks.
Detailed original runtime/static findings integrated into partial C++/SDL3 components. Inspected structured map/player/level state; DOS and Win16 evidence are separately bounded.
Native game-record/rules engine for German disk1.4 and German/English CD editions. Inspected original blood/organ-bank quirks and documented safety fallbacks.
Java21/LWJGL/SDL3 framework includes substantive DOOM game-source port with original fixed-point simulation and named action dispatch. Inspected actor/weapon callback mapping.
Structured Rust game flow/rules and fixed-point software renderer ported from original C, with async waits for browser host. Inspected top-level state orchestration and source routine citations.

Functional Deluxe Paint-inspired editor with original disk assets and standard format readers, but openly adapted algorithms/UI and no recovered original painting algorithm evidence established. Keep application-remake lead; do not mislabel as decompilation.

Static 68000-to-C instruction recompilation plus emulated Amiga hardware; translation tooling useful but not recovered high-level game engine. Retain architecture audit, not native semantic-source promotion.
Modern language-model neuron steering research, not retro golf game or requested platform source recovery. Search collision.

Useful Ghidra/VROOM analysis pipeline, but playable product translates every p-code instruction over emulated8086state; decompiled pseudocode remains noncompilable. Keep analysis/recompilation lead, not recovered native C game.

Current product explicitly executes remaining68000instructions through shared/amigaport interpreter; old static translator removed and gameplay conformance still open. Earlier screenshots do not prove present interpreter completeness.

decisions.reason: Alien Breed SE92, II and Tower Assault asset readers/editor plus ECS engine. Inspected MAPReader handling big-endian chunks and three format identities; EPF and ACBM/SPR/BLK resources supported.

decisions.title: MUI-Builder — Qt6 application reconstruction
decisions.reason: Source-derived Qt6 redesign of Eric Totels MUI-Builder2.3; inspected original version-tag loader mapping and MUIB record parsing. Generates Amiga MUI C source.

decisions.title: Lands of Lore — Go recovered-engine port
decisions.reason: Go/Ebiten source translation from memmaker lands-of-lore-1-re, with structured combat factors and original routine references. EMC/TIM/AV are recovered game-script VMs, not x86 execution.

decisions.title: NHL 95 PC — exact assembly and partial matching C
decisions.reason: Watcom10 LE/DOS4GW recovery with304 assembly segments and977 of1084 functions reported C-matched. Inspected actual DrawFrameSprite C and C progress ledger.

decisions.title: Master of Orion II — partial recovered C++ SDL3 engine
decisions.reason: Original decompiler output incrementally receives real types, native allocation and SDL3 service boundary. Inspected startup/game function recovery rather than instruction-dispatch emulation.

decisions.title: Terep2 — C++ vehicle-physics source reconstruction
decisions.reason: Readable soft-body vehicle simulation derived from original assembly and Win16 port; inspected structured mass-point/spring physics rather than mechanical instruction wrappers.

decisions.title: SkyNET and Future Shock — C# SDL3 reconstruction
decisions.reason: Native engine/editor uses decoded SKYNET.EXE tables and AIS scripts, with prior Godot port as reference. Inspected structured enemy families and original-address perception constants.

decisions.title: F-117A Nighthawk — recovered native C SDL3 port
decisions.reason: Function-by-function simulation/frontend/debrief recovery, inspected original-address-cited award/ribbon implementation. Native services with OPL audio chip model, not original CPU runtime.

decisions.title: Whiplash / Fatal Racing — ROLLER native recovery
decisions.reason: Native recovered/partly rewritten engine with debug-symbol-assisted function identification. Inspected structured car state and bounded numeric conversion, not original x86 execution.

decisions.title: Goldbox Engine — bounded SSI format and ECL recovery
decisions.reason: C++20 DAX/GEO/ECL readers and typed ECL interpreter with terminal exploration and mod overlay framework. Inspected bounded operand/memory access semantics and explicit host callbacks.

decisions.title: Nitemare 3D — DOS/Win16 research and partial C++ engine
decisions.reason: Detailed original runtime/static findings integrated into partial C++/SDL3 components. Inspected structured map/player/level state; DOS and Win16 evidence are separately bounded.

decisions.title: Biing! — C11 SDL3 recovered engine and trainer
decisions.reason: Native game-record/rules engine for German disk1.4 and German/English CD editions. Inspected original blood/organ-bank quirks and documented safety fallbacks.

decisions.title: Inferno Engine — Java DOOM source port and format framework
decisions.reason: Java21/LWJGL/SDL3 framework includes substantive DOOM game-source port with original fixed-point simulation and named action dispatch. Inspected actor/weapon callback mapping.

decisions.title: Speed Haste — Rust engine and web/native port
decisions.reason: Structured Rust game flow/rules and fixed-point software renderer ported from original C, with async waits for browser host. Inspected top-level state orchestration and source routine citations.

decisions.title: olivierh59500/pixeluxe
decisions.reason: Functional Deluxe Paint-inspired editor with original disk assets and standard format readers, but openly adapted algorithms/UI and no recovered original painting algorithm evidence established. Keep application-remake lead; do not mislabel as decompilation.

decisions.title: SirL0LL0/RockStarAteMyHamsterRecomp
decisions.reason: Static 68000-to-C instruction recompilation plus emulated Amiga hardware; translation tooling useful but not recovered high-level game engine. Retain architecture audit, not native semantic-source promotion.

decisions.title: arthurmateu/neuron-golf
decisions.reason: Modern language-model neuron steering research, not retro golf game or requested platform source recovery. Search collision.

decisions.title: haraldF/wc-decomp
decisions.reason: Useful Ghidra/VROOM analysis pipeline, but playable product translates every p-code instruction over emulated8086state; decompiled pseudocode remains noncompilable. Keep analysis/recompilation lead, not recovered native C game.

decisions.title: SomeoneIsWorking/benefactor
decisions.reason: Current product explicitly executes remaining68000instructions through shared/amigaport interpreter; old static translator removed and gameplay conformance still open. Earlier screenshots do not prove present interpreter completeness.
